extracted.intended_audience: U.S. legislators, USPTO officials, patent practitioners, and patent stakeholders (inventors, universities, companies)
extracted.subtask_description: Legislative and administrative rules and procedural requirements for implementing the America Invents Act and restructuring USPTO funding and operations. Covers funding mechanisms, procedural reforms (post-grant review, supplemental examination), operational targets, reporting, and other statutory changes affecting patent quality and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition to first-inventor-to-file system
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition the U.S. patent system to a first-inventor-to-file regime as part of the America Invents Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a reform to improve the patent process and reduce litigation costs; intended to give clearer incentives to innovate and reduce burdens on small inventors and companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of a post-grant review procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a statutory post-grant review process allowing challenges to issued patents after grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a change that will decrease litigation costs and improve patent quality by providing a post-issuance mechanism to resolve validity and related issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO rulemaking authority to set/adjust fees for seven years
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the USPTO with authority to set or adjust its own fees for seven years without requiring statutory change for each adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to give the agency greater flexibility and control over funding, enabling multi-year planning and operational stability; reduces reliance on frequent statutory fee changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination process for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow patent holders to request a supplemental examination if new information arises after the initial examination, so the USPTO may consider, reconsider, or correct information believed relevant to the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to remove uncertainty in litigation and enhance patent quality; explicitly does not limit USPTO authority to investigate misconduct or sanction bad actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism for third-party submissions during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a mechanism for third parties to submit relevant information during the patent examination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to leverage public knowledge to improve the quality of examination and increase efficiency by providing examiners with better information about the technology and claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of USPTO Public Enterprise (revolving) Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Enterprise Fund (revolving fund) in the Treasury with amounts available to the Director without fiscal year limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments change references to make fees available until expended and move USPTO funding into a revolving-style fund to enable multi-year, business-like planning and reduce dependence on annual appropriations uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation and deposit of fee resources into Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify which fees are to be deposited into the Fund (fees collected under 35 U.S.C. sections 41, 42, 376 and section 31 of the Trademark Act), with stated exceptions for certain enacted-fee provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly excludes fees collected pursuant to specified statutory sections (e.g., section 9(h) of the Act or Public Law 111-45 section 1(a)(2)); Director transfers collected amounts to the Fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenses eligible from the Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts deposited into the Fund shall be available, without fiscal year limitation, to cover expenses consistent with limits on fee use, including administrative and operating expenses the Under Secretary deems ordinary and reasonable, and all expenses pursuant to obligations of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund may be used broadly to support continued operation of services, programs, activities, and duties relating to patents and trademarks as described in title 35 and the Trademark Act of 1946.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report to Congress requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the Under Secretary and Director to submit an annual report to Congress within 60 days after fiscal year end summarizing operations and financials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must: (1) summarize operations including financial details and staff levels broken down by each major activity; (2) detail the operating plan including specific expense and staff needs for the upcoming fiscal year; (3) describe long-term modernization plans; (4) set forth progress toward modernization made in the previous fiscal year; and (5) include results of the most recent audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual spending plan notification and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Director must notify the House and Senate Committees on Appropriations not later than 30 days after the start of each fiscal year of the plan for obligation and expenditure of total funds for that fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each plan must summarize operations for the current fiscal year including financial details and staff levels with respect to major activities and detail the operating plan including specific expense and staff needs for the current fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent annual audit of financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Require an independent audit of the Office's financial statements annually, conducted in accordance with generally acceptable accounting procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audits are to be provided by the Under Secretary on an annual basis; audit results must be included in the annual report to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund prepares and submits business-type budget to the President
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund shall prepare and submit each year to the President a business-type budget in the manner and before the date prescribed by the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to align Fund budgeting with executive budgeting processes and support multi-year planning and fiscal management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharge crediting to the Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts collected pursuant to the surcharge imposed under the Act shall be credited to the United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Enterprise Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that surcharge revenues augment the Fund's resources and are available for USPTO purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO strategic performance targets (pendency and backlog)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set multi-year strategic targets to reduce patent pendency and backlog: first-action pendency to 10 months, final-action pendency to 20 months, and backlog reduction to 350,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are stated goals in the USPTO Strategic Plan and FY 2012 budget submission; achieving them is tied to staffing increases, IT modernization, and efficiency initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity increases: examiner hiring and overtime
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to hire additional patent examiners (1,000 in FY2012 and 1,000 in FY2013) and to use full overtime to increase examination capacity and reduce backlog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hiring and overtime are presented as necessary complements to efficiency gains to meet pendency and backlog goals; plan anticipates eventual moderation of workforce once steady state is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees must be used for services paid for (no fee diversion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that user fees paid by applicants and other stakeholders should be spent to perform the services for which they were paid and not diverted to unrelated government purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative amendments and the Fund aim to prevent historical fee diversion (examples cited include PTO, SEC, Nuclear Waste Fund, Crime Victims Fund) and to provide certainty for multi-year planning and implementation of reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional oversight and accountability expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Congressional oversight should actively review USPTO operations and finances (what was started, what ended, how much spent, where spent, employee turnover, productivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oversight is described as necessary to ensure funds are used properly and to inform potential changes in fee authority or other statutory provisions; lack of oversight has been criticized as a cause of poor accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to funding provisions take effect on the later of October 1, 2011 or the first day of the first fiscal year that begins after enactment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a clear statutory effective date trigger to coordinate fiscal-year implementation of funding changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations/exceptions on fees deposited into Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify that certain fees (for example, fees under section 9(h) of the Act or section 1(a)(2) of Public Law 111-45) shall not be deposited into the Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative text explicitly carves out exceptions to the fees that flow into the Fund to respect other statutory earmarks or special treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenses must be ordinary, reasonable, and consistent with fee-use limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenses charged to the Fund must be consistent with statutory limits on the use of fees and be ordinary and reasonable as determined by the Under Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an administrative constraint intended to prevent misuse of fee revenues while allowing operational flexibility to run USPTO programs and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change to best mode disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative change to the 'best mode' disclosure requirement in patent law is included as part of the America Invents Act reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited among essential improvements intended to modernize the patent system; specifics of the change are part of the bill's substantive patent-law amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expansion of prior user rights defense (with university exemption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand the prior user rights defense to affiliates while exempting university-owned patents from that expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to balance protection for prior commercial users with university technology-transfer and commercialization interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives for government laboratories to commercialize inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Create incentives for government laboratories to commercialize inventions they develop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative provision intended to encourage technology transfer from government research to the private sector, supporting commercialization and public benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on false marking claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Impose restrictions on false marking claims to reduce abusive litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of suite of reforms aimed at curbing frivolous or opportunistic lawsuits tied to false marking allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of residency restrictions for Federal Circuit judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove statutory restrictions on the residency of judges serving on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A structural judicial provision included with patent reforms to affect the composition/availability of the Federal Circuit bench.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of patent-eligibility for tax strategy patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the treatment of tax strategy patents under the patent statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included to address uncertainty and litigation surrounding patents that claim tax strategies; intended to provide clearer boundaries on patentability in this domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance to small businesses through a patent ombudsman
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide assistance to small businesses by establishing a patent ombudsman program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ombudsman is intended to help small entities navigate the patent system and reduce barriers to protection and enforcement of intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of additional USPTO satellite offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorize establishment of additional USPTO satellite offices to improve access and service delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satellite offices intended to broaden geographic reach of USPTO services and support stakeholders across different regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination does not limit USPTO investigatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental examination provision does not limit the USPTO's authority to investigate misconduct or to sanction bad actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that providing supplemental review pathways does not remove enforcement or investigatory powers of the agency.
